title: Jump game II
statement: From index 0, a jump from i can land anywhere in (i, i + nums[i]]. The last index is always reachable. Return the minimum number of jumps to reach it.
hints: Think BFS: layer d is the set of indices reachable in exactly d jumps; each layer is a contiguous range.
Track the end of the current layer and the farthest reach from inside it.

solution.explanation: This is BFS where every layer is an interval of indices, so no queue is needed: scanning the current layer computes the next layer's right end (the farthest reach). When i passes the current layer's end, you've used one more jump. Seeing a greedy as a compressed BFS (or DP) is how you prove it, instead of hoping.
